stories.title: Malaysia's middle path between China and US faces new tests
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has spent much of his time in office insisting that Kuala Lumpur will not be forced to choose between the United States and China. But two sets of comments last month have raised questions about how sustainable that position is as rivalry between the two superpowers increasingly spills into Southeast Asia. "I see Taiwan as part of China, period," he said in an interview with news outlet Al Jazeera that aired on August 16. Beijing considers democratically governed Taiwan part of its territory. While Chinese leaders say they favor "peaceful reunification," they have never ruled out using force to bring the island under Beijing's control. More controversially, Anwar appeared to accept Beijing's argument that force could be necessary. "If one province decides to break away. Do we use force? I think I will, [to] protect the sanctity and unity of the nation," he said. The comments drew an enthusiastic response from Beijing, while Taiwan's Foreign Ministry accused Anwar of effectively legitimizing the use of force against the islandand warned that his "one-sided support for China could negatively impact Taiwanese businesses' confidence in investing in Malaysia," including in the country's strategically important semiconductor sector. Two days after his comments on Taiwan aired, Anwar argued that Malaysiashould strengthen its defenses in Sabah, citing the expansion of US-backed military facilities on the nearby Philippine island of Balabac. The Philippines is upgrading facilities on Balabac, roughly 50 kilometers (31 miles) from the Malaysian islands of Banggi and Balambangan.

stories.title: Gazprom shares extend gains amid plans to discuss Power of Siberia 2 project with China
stories.summary: By 1:53 p.m. Moscow time, the price of the company’s shares had extended gains to 2.24% reaching 89.9 rubles per share
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 3.

Gazprom shares extended gains on the Moscow Exchange, having gained more than 2% following Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak’s statement on plans to discuss the Power of Siberia 2 project at a meeting of the Russia-China intergovernmental commission on Friday, according to trading data.
As of 1:44 p.m. Moscow time (10:44 a.m. GMT), the price of Gazprom shares was up by 0.72% at 88.56 rubles per share.
By 1:53 p.m. Moscow time (10:53 a.m. GMT), the price of the company’s shares had extended gains to 2.24% reaching 89.9 rubles per share.

Novak said in an interview with the Vesti program earlier that the route and commercial terms for gas supplies under the Power of Siberia 2 project would be discussed at a meeting of the intergovernmental commission on the development of trade and economic relations with China on Friday.

stories.summary: Across the world, hundreds of people have come to believe they have made extraordinary scientific discoveries with AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. stories.title: Kalashnikov unveils upgraded Skat 350M drone at exhibition in Kazan
stories.summary: The upgraded Skat 350M is equipped with a thermal imager and a highly sensitive camera, both mounted on a single gyro-stabilized platform
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 3.
The Kalashnikov Group has presented a modernized version of its Skat 350M drone at the Integrated Security exhibition in Kazan, the company’s press service told TASS.

"The Skat 350M unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), manufactured by the Kalashnikov Group, which can simultaneously detect and track objects emitting heat and visible light, is on display at the 16th International Salon ‘Integrated Security’ in Kazan.
The UAV will significantly improve the effectiveness of rescue services in searching for missing persons," the company said in a statement.

The upgraded Skat 350M is equipped with a thermal imager and a highly sensitive camera, both mounted on a single gyro-stabilized platform, which allows for continuous surveillance of a target at any time of day or night without losing sight of it.
"We can confidently say that rescue services now have new technical capabilities.

Our drone, equipped with both a thermal imager and a highly sensitive camera, is capable of detecting any objects at night that emit thermal radiation or visible light, for example, a car with its headlights on but a cold engine, or the light from a flashlight in the hand of a victim," said Leonid Rokeakh, the group’s international business director.
